precedents.signature_overlap: host.memory.exhaustion on a batch integration host; batch transfers running late; no transfers failed.
precedents.divergence: INC-2411 was resolved by correlating the exhaustion with a recent JVM heap tuning change and reverting it. precedents.falsifying_test: If process-level memory attribution shows the JVM heap — not the audit analysis daemon — is the dominant memory consumer, INC-2411 becomes the closer match; if the daemon dominates, it does not apply.

incident_ref.heading_path: INC-2288: Sustained CPU from an OS denial-analysis daemon > Timeline

precedents.signature_overlap: Audit analysis daemon active and consuming CPU; high denial volume keeping the daemon resident; security module generating real denials.
precedents.divergence: Platform security standard SEC-STD-14 (2026-01-30) requires the audit event dispatcher to remain active on production hosts. Deactivating it is no longer an available resolution, and doing it here destroyed the evidence that would have identified the source domain. Additionally, INC-2288 did not involve host memory exhaustion or late batch transfers; the current incident carries both. The audit denial log naming the source domain — the evidence that would distinguish candidates — is outstanding here as it was in INC-2288.
precedents.resolution_taken: INC-2288 record states the audit event dispatcher was deactivated so the denial stream no longer reached the analysis daemon.
precedents.falsifying_test: If the audit denial log, when produced, shows no elevated denial volume during the affected window, the daemon's CPU consumption has a different driver and INC-2288 does not apply.
